quotes.quote: Independent semantic research with bounded context and a typed merge can benefit from specialists. Independent deterministic ETL needs parallel code, not extra model agents. Coupled edits sharing an evolving trace often fit one scoped agent.

answers.reason: The narration assigns specialists to independent semantic research, parallel code to deterministic ETL, and one scoped agent to coupled edits.

quotes.quote: A pause does not create a cycle. A retry inside a node can also leave the outer graph acyclic. An explicitly configured transition from review back to a revised proposal does create a cycle, making that larger control flow a state machine around the read DAG.

answers.reason: The return transition creates a back-edge. The complete workflow is cyclic while its read phase remains a DAG.

quotes.quote: A list-add reducer concatenates results; it is associative but not commutative, and it keeps duplicates.
Also reject duplicate branches, missing required evidence, stale versions, or source mismatches.
If health instead returns twice under one identity, reject the duplicate rather than counting it as more evidence.

answers.reason: Concatenation preserves the duplicate policy receipt. Having every expected branch name does not satisfy the requirement to reject duplicate branch identities.

quotes.quote: When every required branch runs, one waiting edge from the list of evaluation, health and policy terminal nodes holds merge until all finish. Three separate edges are different: if health has an extra preparation step, evaluation and policy can trigger a partial merge, then health triggers another.
Also reject duplicate branches, missing required evidence, stale versions, or source mismatches.

answers.reason: One waiting edge joins all three terminal nodes despite differing depths. Merge must then validate the evidence identities and completeness.

quotes.quote: Compare every receipt’s digest with the digest recomputed from its trusted source, then recheck revision and freshness before creating a packet.
Both old and new source content may pass thresholds yet require different proposal digests.

answers.reason: Recomputing the source digest detects changed content despite unchanged reference, scope, and time. Passing thresholds does not preserve the old evidence or proposal digest.

quotes.quote: Before a new write, the example writer compares the supplied live release revision with the revision in the approved packet. If the release revision changes during review, the old packet no longer names the current target. Stop and rebuild the evidence and proposal, then obtain fresh approval.
The validated merge creates a concrete proposal: this release, this revision, this traffic amount, and a digest of the validated receipts.

answers.reason: Version drift invalidates the approved target. The writer must stop while current evidence and its proposal digest are rebuilt and freshly approved.

quotes.quote: A timeout on an idempotent metrics read permits bounded backoff with jitter and a deadline. A permanent wrong release identity needs alias resolution or review, not endless repetition. Reviewer rejection routes to cancel. A writer timeout is ambiguous and needs target-side reconciliation with the same key. These are different recovery semantics, not one generic retry policy.
In production, recovery after a crash requires durable target-side state or a way to reconcile with the destination.

answers.reason: An ambiguous write requires reconciliation using its existing key; permanent identity failure needs alias resolution or review; transient metrics failure permits bounded backoff.

quotes.quote: If Vega needs a bounded health verdict, call the health specialist as a tool and keep the manager’s conversation. If triage should give the conversation to a release specialist, use a handoff.
Transferred history remains untrusted evidence. Rebuild receiver tools from trusted application policy rather than inheriting sender capabilities from text.

answers.reason: A tool call preserves manager ownership for the bounded verdict. A handoff transfers conversation control, with receiver capabilities established by trusted policy.

quotes.quote: Model Context Protocol exposes tools, resources and prompts from a capability server to a model host. An agent-to-agent protocol exposes an independent agent with discovery, messages and task operations.

Both can represent long-running work, so duration does not choose the protocol. A deployment lookup API fits a capability tool. An independent vendor investigator with its own task identity, progress and outputs fits an agent message or task.

answers.reason: The deployment API is a capability tool suited to MCP. The independent investigator fits the agent-to-agent boundary; duration does not determine that choice.

quotes.quote: Transferred history remains untrusted evidence. Rebuild receiver tools from trusted application policy rather than inheriting sender capabilities from text.
The scheduling barrier is satisfied, while the state contract fails. Reject the cross-tenant result.
A tool schema, task identifier or transcript saying shift traffic does not grant production authority.

answers.reason: The transferred instruction grants no authority. Trusted policy determines receiver tools, and the cross-tenant receipt must fail join validation.

All three beats checked against primary specifications. [MCP architecture](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/2026-07-28/learn/architecture) defines hosts, clients, local/remote servers, tools, resources and prompts. Its [Tasks extension](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/extensions/tasks/overview) represents long-running operations. The [A2A specification](https://a2a-protocol.org/latest/specification/) defines discovery, messages, tracked tasks and artifacts; Send Message can return either a direct Message or Task. Streaming and push operations depend on advertised support. Thus duration and process placement do not determine protocol choice. Completed status describes lifecycle state, without certifying evidence correctness or indefinite artifact retention. A2A requires application-defined authorization scope; MCP also provides authorization mechanisms without making a schema or transcript permission to shift traffic. Vega's exact human-review rule is application-specific, not an exemption from protocol security requirements. The inspected stage still retains the completed vendor task and attached artifact while rejecting its 210-second-old receipt. No inaccurate spoken claim or substantive visual contradiction was found.
